purpose: Review historical and recent fish-diversity sources for Buguey Lagoon without converting incomplete publication summaries into a public species checklist.

siteLead.waterbodyClass: Lagoon described by the recent study as coastal and connected toward an estuary; the Villa Leonora station is at the lagoon mouth where salinity is high.
identityAndCoverageLimits: The 2024 study names Villa Leonora, Centro and Cabaritan as sampling locations, but provides no station coordinates or reusable lagoon boundary.
The 2015 conference-abstract index says three sites/barangays but does not name the three sites.

The records do not resolve whether the 2015, 2024 and 2026 source outputs refer to independent field campaigns or overlapping data. The latter two share an author, location and similar sampling method, but no collection period or dataset identifier establishes their relationship.

Do not classify Buguey Lagoon as a freshwater lake solely because the 2015 abstract index calls it inland water; the recent study describes an estuary-facing high-salinity station. Keep its salinity and habitat extent unverified outside those source descriptions.

studyEvidence.studyIdentity: CSU-funded project titled Assessment of Species Diversity of Fishes in Buguey Lagoon, implemented by Cagayan State University–Aparri Campus; the brief names Quirino G. Pascua and Jasper Allain B. Argonza on the project team.
studyEvidence.sourceReportedFinding: The 2026 brief reports 56 finfish species in 40 families and says Gobiidae has the highest finfish richness. It names Ambassis gymnocephalus, Mugil cephalus and Glossogobius aureus in its summary of dominant or abundant catch. It states that preparation of a fish-species compendium for communities is an intervention still to be made.
studyEvidence.methodsAndSites: The brief describes Villa Leonora (mouth/estuary), Centro (east of bridge) and Cabaritan (west of fish port); sampling from fyke-net catches of three fishers in each selected barangay, three times per month from 2:00–8:00 AM. The brief does not state the collection years or dates.
limitations: The brief does not contain the full 56-species checklist, taxon-by-site rows, specimen vouchers, counts by taxon, or exact sampling coordinates.

Its methods resemble the 2024 JBES paper, which has the same author, three localities and sampling frequency, but no field dates or shared dataset identifier was found; treat their relationship and differing reported results as unresolved.
A proposal to designate a protected area in a policy brief is not proof that a legal protected-area designation or fishing rule has been enacted.

studyEvidence.studyIdentity: Quirino G. Pascua, Assessment on species diversity of fishes in Buguey Lagoon, Cagayan, Northern Philippines, Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Sciences, 24(3), 135–141; published 2024-03-17.
studyEvidence.methodsAndSites: The full article describes Villa Leonora near the lagoon mouth/estuary, Centro east of the bridge, and Cabaritan west of the fish port. It reports fyke-net landing-site samples from three fishers in each barangay, three times monthly from 2:00–8:00 AM. No sampling date range is stated in the reviewed text.
studyEvidence.finding: The paper reports diversity indices and a cross-site similarity result but the reviewed seven-page article does not provide a named species checklist or taxon-by-station records. Its open-access label is not an item-specific reuse license.
limitations: No source-linked species names, vouchers, specimen accessions, exact station coordinates or field dates were found in the reviewed article.
The article's ecological and pollution interpretations are not adopted as current water-quality, safety, population or habitat-status claims.

studyEvidence.studyIdentity: Search-indexed abstract titled Species Diversity of Finfishes and Crustaceans of Buguey Lagoon by Wilma S. Urmeneta and Ramil T. Romias; its conference year and a retrievable primary copy were not verified.
studyEvidence.sourceReportedFinding: The indexed abstract reports sampling twice monthly from June through November 2015 at three sites/barangays, with 55 total taxa: 43 finfishes, six shrimp and six crab species. It names Portunus pelagicus, Ambassys gymnocephalus, Penaeus indicus and Litopeneaus vannamei in the indexed text.
limitations: The ILEC-hosted PDF URL was unavailable in the reviewed access attempt and the web reader redirected to an unrelated file; only the search-engine indexed abstract text was available.
The three sites are not named in the indexed abstract, and it provides no voucher or taxon-by-site list.
Preserve Ambassys and Litopeneaus exactly as indexed; do not silently normalize these spellings or merge them with later names until the original source and taxonomic crosswalk are checked.
The 2015 aggregate count is historical and cannot be used as a current or complete lagoon checklist.

crossSourceDiscrepancies: The 2015 indexed abstract reports 43 finfishes (55 total finfish and crustacean taxa), while the 2026 CSU brief reports 56 finfish species. Their campaigns may be different, but no full 2015 abstract, exact site crosswalk, 2024/2026 field dates or dataset identifiers were retrieved to resolve the discrepancy.

The older indexed spelling Ambassys gymnocephalus differs from the 2026 brief's Ambassis gymnocephalus. Do not treat the labels as reconciled until the primary checklist and accepted-name authority are checked.

The 2026 CSU article page displays CC BY 4.0, while its downloadable PDF states that all rights are reserved and prior permission is required. Treat redistribution rights as unresolved; no checklist or PDF content is copied into Bangwit.

gbifScreen.interpretation: One exact indexed waterBody filter only. A zero result does not show that fish, surveys, or GBIF records are absent under alternate locality names or fields.

interpretationLimits: Do not promote source-reported taxa or aggregate counts to public current-presence, abundance, native status, catchability, natural-diet, conservation-status or legal claims without the primary checklist, sampling dates, voucher/taxonomic review and item-specific rights decision.
Do not infer the lagoon shoreline, municipal-water boundary, salinity throughout the lagoon, fishing access, safety, water quality or a protected-area boundary from these papers.
Fish-diversity and human catch data are not equivalent to full ecosystem inventories; the sources also discuss crustaceans, which need separate taxonomic coverage.
followUp: Request the full 2015 abstract/paper, all species tables, taxon-by-station counts, vouchers or collection identifiers, exact survey dates and site names from the authors or Cagayan State University.

Ask CSU for the complete dataset underlying the 56-fin-fish summary, its field dates, exact relation to Pascua (2024), accepted-name list, voucher/accession details, and written reuse terms for app display.
Resolve the two reported finfish counts and the Ambassys/Ambassis spelling with the primary sources and an accepted taxonomic authority before creating any species rows.

Crosswalk Villa Leonora, Centro and Cabaritan to official barangay and hydrographic features; obtain a reusable lagoon polygon and estuary connection reference from NAMRIA/LGU, without assuming that a map illustration is a GIS boundary.
Confirm whether any protected-area or fishery rule was formally enacted by retrieving the cited municipal ordinance or resolution; do not encode the brief's proposed action as current law.

sources.supports: CSU 2026 policy brief: 56 source-reported finfish species, 40 families, a few named taxa, three study barangays and fyke-net sampling method; no full checklist or field date range in the brief.
Full 2024 fish-diversity article reviewed for its study sites, method and limits; no species checklist or sampling date range was found in the article.
Search-indexed conference abstract lead reporting the 2015 survey period and aggregate finfish/crustacean counts; direct document access failed, so this remains provisional.
Single exact-field GBIF occurrence screen returned count 0; not absence evidence.
Region II inland-water inventory updated with Buguey Lagoon as a separate estuary-connected lagoon/fish-survey lead; no public records or geometry added.
